questions.stem: What is the preferred format for a Snowflake account identifier?

options.text: Account locator with region and cloud platform
Organization name followed by the account name
Email address of the account administrator
Cloud platform region code followed by account locator

explanation.correct: The preferred account identifier format is the organization name followed by the account name (e.g., myorg-account123). The account locator format is legacy and its use is discouraged.

distractors.A: The account locator format with region and cloud is the legacy format — its use is discouraged.
distractors.C: Email addresses are not used as account identifiers.
distractors.D: Region code followed by locator is not a valid identifier format.

questions.stem: How long does a Snowflake trial account last?

options.text: 60 days or until free credits are exhausted
14 days regardless of credit consumption
30 days or until free credits are exhausted, whichever comes first
90 days with unlimited credits

explanation.correct: A Snowflake trial continues for 30 days from the sign-up date or until the free usage balance is depleted, whichever occurs first.

distractors.A: The trial period is 30 days, not 60 days.
distractors.B: 14 days is incorrect, and the trial does end early if credits are exhausted.
distractors.D: The trial is 30 days (not 90) and credits are limited, not unlimited.

questions.stem: What is the maximum character length for a Snowflake account identifier string, including organization name, account name, and separator?

options.text: 128 characters
32 characters
63 characters
255 characters

explanation.correct: The account identifier string length, including the organization name, account name, and separator characters, should not exceed 63 characters.

distractors.A: 128 characters exceeds the actual limit of 63.
distractors.B: 32 characters is too restrictive — the actual limit is 63.
distractors.D: 255 characters far exceeds the actual limit of 63.

questions.stem: Which requirements apply to Snowflake account identifiers? (Select THREE)

options.text: Must be unique within an organization regardless of region
Can contain special characters including @ and #
Must start with an alphabetic character
Can contain underscores but should not end with one
Must include the cloud platform code
Must be at least 8 characters long

explanation.correct: Account identifiers must be unique within an organization (regardless of region), must start with an alphabetic character, and can contain underscores but should not end with one.

distractors.B: Account identifiers cannot contain special characters except underscores — @ and # are not allowed.
distractors.E: The cloud platform code is not part of the preferred account identifier format.
distractors.F: There is no minimum length requirement of 8 characters for account identifiers.

questions.stem: Which features are NOT available for Snowflake trial accounts? (Select TWO)

options.text: Virtual warehouses
External network access
Loading data from cloud storage
Hybrid tables
Creating databases and schemas

explanation.correct: External network access and hybrid tables are among the current limitations for trial accounts. Virtual warehouses, data loading, and creating databases are all available during trial.

distractors.A: Virtual warehouses are available and are the primary way to consume trial credits.
distractors.C: Loading data from cloud storage (S3, Azure, GCS) is fully supported in trial accounts.
distractors.E: Creating databases and schemas is a basic feature available in all accounts including trial.

questions.stem: Which of the following are types of Snowflake parameters? (Select THREE)

options.text: Network parameters
Account parameters
Session parameters
Object parameters
User parameters
Security parameters

explanation.correct: Snowflake provides three types of parameters: account parameters (affect the entire account), session parameters (default to users and their sessions), and object parameters (default to warehouses, databases, schemas, and tables).

distractors.A: Network parameters is not one of the three Snowflake parameter types.
distractors.E: User parameters is not a distinct category — users are affected by session parameters.
distractors.F: Security parameters is not a distinct category in Snowflake's parameter hierarchy.

questions.scenario: A company uses Okta as their identity provider and has a Snowflake account named 'data_warehouse' in the organization 'acme'. They are configuring the SSO integration URL.
questions.stem: What URL format must they use for the Okta SSO configuration?

options.text: https://acme-data_warehouse.snowflakecomputing.com
https://acme-data-warehouse.snowflakecomputing.com
https://acme.data_warehouse.snowflakecomputing.com
https://data_warehouse.acme.snowflakecomputing.com

explanation.correct: Okta does not support underscores in URLs. When using Okta, underscores in the account name must be converted to hyphens, resulting in acme-data-warehouse.snowflakecomputing.com.

distractors.A: This format contains an underscore which Okta does not support in URLs.
distractors.C: This uses a dot separator between org and account which is not the correct URL format.
distractors.D: This reverses the order (account before org) and uses a dot separator, which is incorrect.

questions.scenario: A network engineer is setting up AWS PrivateLink connectivity to their Snowflake account. The organization is 'techcorp' and the account name is 'proddb'.
questions.stem: What is the correct URL format for private connectivity?

options.text: https://techcorp-proddb.private.snowflakecomputing.com
https://techcorp-proddb.snowflakecomputing.com/privatelink
https://techcorp-proddb.privatelink.snowflakecomputing.com
https://private.techcorp-proddb.snowflakecomputing.com

explanation.correct: For private connectivity, the string 'privatelink' must be appended to the account identifier in the URL, resulting in orgname-account_name.privatelink.snowflakecomputing.com.

distractors.B: The privatelink keyword is placed between the identifier and snowflakecomputing.com, not as a path suffix.
distractors.D: The privatelink keyword goes after the account identifier, not before it.

questions.scenario: A data engineer's trial account has been suspended because the 30-day period expired. They still need to access the data they loaded during the trial.
questions.stem: What must they do to reactivate the suspended trial account?

options.text: Contact Snowflake Support to extend the trial period
Create a new trial account and transfer the data
Enter a credit card to convert it to a paid account
Wait 24 hours for the account to automatically reactivate

explanation.correct: To reactivate a suspended trial account, you must enter a credit card, which converts it to a paid account. You can still log into a suspended account but cannot use features until converted.

distractors.A: Snowflake Support does not extend trial periods — conversion to paid is required.
distractors.B: Creating a new trial account would not give access to the data in the original suspended account.
distractors.D: Suspended trial accounts do not automatically reactivate — payment information is required.

questions.scenario: An account administrator wants to view all account-level parameters and their current values to audit the account configuration.
questions.stem: Which SQL command should they use?

options.text: DESCRIBE ACCOUNT PARAMETERS;
LIST PARAMETERS FOR ACCOUNT;
SHOW PARAMETERS IN ACCOUNT;
SELECT * FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PARAMETERS;

explanation.correct: SHOW PARAMETERS IN ACCOUNT displays all parameters and their current values for the account, along with default values and descriptions.

distractors.A: DESCRIBE ACCOUNT PARAMETERS is not valid Snowflake SQL syntax.
distractors.B: LIST PARAMETERS FOR ACCOUNT is not valid Snowflake SQL syntax.
distractors.D: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PARAMETERS does not exist — parameters are viewed using SHOW PARAMETERS.

questions.scenario: A trial account user is trying to conserve their free credits and wants to understand what consumes credits and what doesn't.
questions.stem: Which statements about trial account credit consumption are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Free credits are consumed by queries running on shared compute resources
Free credits are only consumed by virtual warehouses the user creates
Storage costs are also subtracted from the free usage balance
Credits are consumed even when warehouses are suspended
Larger warehouses consume fewer credits due to parallel efficiency

explanation.correct: Free credits are only consumed by virtual warehouses you create (and only when running). Storage costs are also subtracted from the free usage balance based on standard On-Demand rates.

distractors.A: There are no shared compute resources in trial — credits are consumed by your own warehouses.
distractors.D: Credits are only consumed while warehouses are running, not when suspended.
distractors.E: Larger warehouses consume more credits, not fewer — the consumption scales with size.

questions.scenario: A company is using the Client Redirect feature and wants to understand the different URL formats supported for connecting to their Snowflake accounts.
questions.stem: Which URL formats does Snowflake support for connecting to accounts? (Select THREE)

options.text: Account name format using organization and account name
Connection name format for Client Redirect
Account locator format (legacy)
IP address format for direct connectivity
DNS CNAME alias format
Service endpoint format using VPC ID

explanation.correct: Snowflake supports three URL formats: account name (orgname-account_name), connection name (for Client Redirect), and the legacy account locator format (accountlocator.region.cloud).

distractors.D: IP address format is not supported — Snowflake uses domain-based URLs.
distractors.E: DNS CNAME aliases are used for private connectivity DNS setup but are not a Snowflake URL format.
distractors.F: VPC ID-based service endpoint format is not a supported Snowflake URL format.

questions.scenario: A startup added a credit card to their trial account on day 15. They want to understand the billing implications after conversion.
questions.stem: Which statements about converting a trial account to a paid account are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Remaining free credits continue to be usable until the trial period ends
The trial period immediately ends upon adding a credit card
Unused free balance expires when the 30-day trial period ends
The free credits are converted to a permanent billing credit
Conversion requires contacting Snowflake Support

explanation.correct: Adding a credit card converts the trial without ending the trial period. Free credits remain usable during the remainder. However, any unused free balance expires when the trial period ends.

distractors.B: Adding a credit card does NOT end the trial period — free credits can still be used for the remaining days.
distractors.D: Unused credits expire at the end of the trial period — they are not converted to permanent billing credit.
distractors.E: Conversion is self-service — you add a credit card through Snowsight without contacting support.

questions.scenario: A user wants to cancel their Snowflake trial account and is exploring their options.
questions.stem: Which statements about canceling a Snowflake trial account are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Trial accounts can be canceled at any time during the trial
Cancellation is available through the Snowsight web interface
You must contact Snowflake Support to cancel a trial account
Cancellation automatically occurs when the trial period ends
Only accounts with remaining credits can be canceled

explanation.correct: A trial account can be canceled at any time by contacting Snowflake Support. Currently, trial accounts cannot be canceled through the web interface.

distractors.B: Trial cancellation is NOT available through the web interface — you must contact Snowflake Support.
distractors.D: When the trial ends, the account is suspended, not canceled/deleted. It remains accessible for login.
distractors.E: There is no restriction on canceling based on remaining credit balance.

questions.scenario: An account administrator converted their trial account to paid. After the free credits were exhausted, they noticed multiple charges within a single month beyond the expected monthly billing.
questions.stem: Which statements about threshold billing for converted trial accounts are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Threshold payments occur when consumption reaches certain levels before month end
Threshold payments only happen once per calendar month
Email notifications are sent each time a threshold payment is charged
Threshold payments are not credited toward the monthly total
Threshold billing only applies to Enterprise Edition accounts

explanation.correct: Threshold payments are automatically billed when consumption reaches certain thresholds before month end, and can occur multiple times. An email notification is sent each time a threshold payment is charged.

distractors.B: Threshold payments can occur multiple times in a single month — they are not limited to once.
distractors.D: Threshold payments are credited toward that month's total consumption.
distractors.E: Threshold billing applies to all converted trial (ODSS) accounts regardless of edition.

questions.scenario: A Snowflake administrator is overriding session parameter defaults at different levels in the hierarchy.
questions.stem: Which statements about the Snowflake parameter hierarchy are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Only ACCOUNTADMIN can override default values at the account level
Session and object parameters can be overridden at each level in the parameter hierarchy
Account parameters can be overridden at the session level by any user
Object parameters only apply to virtual warehouses
Parameter overrides at lower levels always take precedence over account-level settings

explanation.correct: Only the ACCOUNTADMIN role can override default values at the account level. Session and object parameters have a hierarchy where defaults can be overridden at each level.

distractors.C: Account parameters affect the entire account and are not overridable at session level by regular users.
distractors.D: Object parameters apply to warehouses, databases, schemas, and tables — not only warehouses.
distractors.E: While lower-level overrides generally take precedence, this is an oversimplification — the behavior depends on the specific parameter.

questions.scenario: A company's Snowflake account has the identifier 'analytics_hub' in the organization 'globalcorp'. A new team member needs to find the organization and account name but does not have the ORGADMIN role.
questions.stem: How can the team member find the organization and account name?

options.text: Execute SHOW ACCOUNTS to list all accounts in the organization
Use the account selector in Snowsight and select 'View account details'
Query the ORGANIZATION_USAGE.ACCOUNTS view
Contact the organization administrator since this information requires ORGADMIN

explanation.correct: Any user can find the organization and account name through Snowsight by opening the account selector and selecting 'View account details', which displays the account identifier and URL.

distractors.A: SHOW ACCOUNTS requires the ORGADMIN or GLOBALORGADMIN role — regular users cannot execute it.
distractors.C: ORGANIZATION_USAGE views require specific privileges not available to all users.
distractors.D: The information is accessible to all users through Snowsight — ORGADMIN is not required.

questions.scenario: A DevOps engineer is setting up multiple Snowflake connections and needs to understand the legacy account locator format for backwards compatibility with older tools.
questions.stem: Which statements about the legacy account locator format are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: The legacy format is no longer supported and will cause connection failures
The legacy format is still supported but its use is discouraged
The legacy URL format is: accountlocator.region.cloud.snowflakecomputing.com
The legacy format includes the organization name as a prefix
The legacy format is required for all private connectivity setups

explanation.correct: The legacy account locator format is still supported for backwards compatibility but its use is discouraged. Its URL format is accountlocator.region.cloud.snowflakecomputing.com.

distractors.A: The legacy format is still supported — it has not been removed.
distractors.D: The legacy format uses the account locator, not the organization name — organization name is part of the preferred format.
distractors.E: Private connectivity works with all URL formats (account name, connection name, and legacy locator).

questions.scenario: A Snowflake user signed up for a trial account selecting Enterprise Edition on AWS in us-east-1. After 20 days, they notice their free credits are nearly exhausted despite moderate usage.
questions.stem: What is the most likely explanation for the rapid credit depletion?

options.text: AWS us-east-1 has higher credit costs than other regions
Enterprise Edition features consume additional credits beyond basic warehouse usage
Trial accounts are charged double the normal credit rate
The 30-day trial period reduces available credits proportionally each day

explanation.correct: When signing up for a trial, the edition selection affects credit consumption. Some features available in Enterprise Edition consume additional credits, which can deplete the balance faster.

distractors.A: While region can affect costs, the documentation specifically notes that edition selection affects how quickly credits are exhausted.
distractors.C: Trial accounts are not charged at double the rate — they use standard credit rates.
distractors.D: Credits are consumed based on actual usage, not reduced proportionally by time.

questions.scenario: A company is using the connection name URL format for Client Redirect. They want to find the name of their connection to configure the URL.
questions.stem: Which SQL command should they execute to find the connection name?

options.text: SHOW CONNECTIONS;
DESCRIBE CONNECTION;
LIST CONNECTIONS IN ACCOUNT;
SELECT * FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.CONNECTIONS;

explanation.correct: The SHOW CONNECTIONS command displays the connections available in the account, which can be used in the connection name URL format for Client Redirect.

distractors.B: DESCRIBE CONNECTION requires specifying a connection name — you would use SHOW CONNECTIONS to find available connections first.
distractors.C: LIST CONNECTIONS IN ACCOUNT is not valid Snowflake SQL syntax.
distractors.D: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.CONNECTIONS does not exist — use SHOW CONNECTIONS instead.
